region.name: Eng Leadership Daily Log
region.summary: Daily engineering leadership notes from mid-2026 covering the ACH pipeline cut-over and Sep 26 idempotency incident, investing GA go/no-go blockers, Series B diligence, VP Eng hiring, Pillar remediation commitments, and team workload concerns.

brief.text:
The Eng Leadership Daily Log is a running set of daily notes from the log's author, an engineering leader, covering mid-to-late 2026 at a fintech with ACH money movement, a round-up savings sweep, an investing product, and planned card issuing. The main technical thread is the migration from the legacy Sidekiq ACH code to an outbox-based pipeline. A Sunday-peak load test at 3x volume failed about 40 minutes in because of outbox table vacuum contention, with no data loss. That failure pushed the ACH cut-over from end of June to Aug 18, with shadow mode running Aug 4-17. Devon Park proposed day-partitioning the outbox table, and Marcus Bell asked for proof before agreeing. The cut-over then completed with the new pipeline as primary, including the first successful NACHA cutoff. A 30-day stability hold was set before anyone touches the old Sidekiq code. Deletion of that code was approved on Sep 17, but Devon still had not deleted it by early October. On Sep 26 there was a SEV1 incident: the round-up sweep had no idempotency key, and a Sidekiq retry change exposed it. The postmortem produced action items and an experiment freeze. ADR-032 moves the round-up sweep onto the outbox pipeline, and Devon wants to lead that build. The idempotency gap on the round-up sweep is still an open severity-5 risk owned by Marcus. The card issuing soft launch has slipped to Q1 2027.

The investing GA is targeted for Oct 20, and that date is an open severity-4 risk owned by Renee. The first go/no-go was a NO-GO with three blockers: the fractional-share reconciliation fix, the disclosures review, and Android parity. Hana later signed off the disclosures, which cleared that blocker. At last report the reconciliation fix was in review and Android parity was about half done. Go/no-go #2 is set for Oct 16. Fractional-share reconciliation drift in the investing beta is a separate open severity-4 risk owned by Devon Park. Pillar remediation commitments also appear in the log. Marcus handed the Pillar weekly sync to Sarah, and the author judged that the draft remediation plan read as defensive and needed a rewrite.

On the business side, Northfield Ventures issued a Series B term sheet for $38M at a $210M post-money valuation. That kicked off technical diligence, data room preparation (scale metrics were the next item), and a plan for 12 engineering hires. The author was also preparing for a diligence call with Elena Sorensen, where key-person risk was a concern. The VP Eng search narrowed to two finalists. Tomas Reyes brings strong money-movement domain experience but raised a concern about a process-heavy culture. Grace Liu had a strong final round on leadership but lacks regulated money-movement experience. Separately, Ama's offer is stuck on compensation because the iOS band sits below market and the offer-accept rate is 55%. Getting that offer through comp approval is an open todo owned by Nadia Okafor. Theo Brandt started during the cut-over period. A recurring theme is leadership bandwidth: Marcus and the author carry nearly every money-movement, fundraising, and hiring thread between them, and the author repeatedly worries that Marcus is overloaded and not doing fine. Typical questions this region answers include why the ACH cut-over slipped, what caused the Sep 26 incident, what is blocking investing GA and who owns each risk, the Series B terms, where the VP Eng candidates stand, and whether the team's workload is sustainable.
